title: Performance and load pack for profile compute, WS fan-out and row rendering
body:
## Context
Profiles are the heaviest read surface in R2: up to 5 000 price rows per period, recomputation on every pan in visible-range mode, composite queries reaching into the cold Parquet/DuckDB tier, and a 1 000 ms-cadence WS topic that `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 8 explicitly degrades first under saturation alongside `heatmap`. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` requires recorded numbers against budgets before a train exits; R2 cannot be declared beta on impressions.

The stories carry hard NFRs: full 24 h rebuild <= 1 s, visible-range recompute <= 10 Hz with >= 55 fps interaction, 30-session composite <= 2 s from the cold tier, re-bucket <= 300 ms in a worker, 5 000 rows rendered.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Engine benchmark** `bench/engine/profile-render.bench.ts`: frame time and fps while panning and zooming with the profile pane open at 500 / 2 000 / 5 000 rows, in volume, delta, TPO and combined modes, at DPR 1 and 2, on the GPU matrix established by the E11/E06 engine baseline. Reports p50/p95/p99 frame time, dropped frames, LOD merge level and GPU memory.
- **Compute benchmark** `bench/profile_engine/`: incremental accumulation throughput (prints/s) at realistic and 10x peak BTCUSDT rates; full 24 h rebuild wall-clock from QuestDB; composite of 5 and 30 sessions from Parquet/DuckDB, cold and warm; re-bucket from `price_grouping` 1 to 50; the cost of the 5 s flush and its effect on ingestion latency.
- **k6 API load script** `load/k6/profile-api.js`: `GET /api/v1/market/profile` with mixed shapes (`split=session|composite|fixed`), concurrency ramped to the R2 target, asserting p95 latency budgets and that bounded-window rejection from `E19-T02` keeps tail latency flat instead of letting one huge query dominate the pool.
- **WS fan-out script** `load/k6/profile-ws.js`: N clients x M symbols subscribed to `profile.{symbol}.{kind}`, verifying the 1 000 ms cadence, coalescing correctness (no lost final state), per-topic sequence continuity, and the documented degradation ladder - at `saturated` the topic drops to 1 000 ms, a `system` notice is emitted and `degraded_topics` names the profile topic.
- **Budget file** `perf/budgets/e19.yaml` encoding every threshold, consumed by CI so a regression fails a job rather than being noticed in a demo.
- **Report** `docs/perf/e19-profiles-report.md`: measured numbers against budgets, hardware matrix, flame-graph highlights and an explicit per-budget verdict (pass, or accepted deviation with owner sign-off and a follow-up ticket).

## Out of scope
- Footprint and heatmap budgets (E18/E21), present here only as background load.
- Optimisation work itself; this ticket measures and files regressions, fixes land on the owning engineering tickets.
- 24 h soak, owned by the E46 performance-hardening epic; scenarios here run <= 60 minutes.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Interaction stays smooth at maximum rows
  Given a 5 000-row profile pane docked beside a chart at DPR 2
  When the user pans and zooms continuously for 60 seconds
  Then p95 frame time is within the 55 fps budget and dropped frames stay under the documented threshold, with LOD merging engaged rather than rows dropped

Scenario: Rebuild and composite budgets are met
  When a full 24 h session profile is rebuilt from QuestDB
  Then it completes in under 1 second
  And a 30-session composite served from the cold tier completes in under 2 seconds

Scenario: Failure case - oversized window is rejected, not absorbed
  Given a request whose window exceeds the bounded-window limit
  Then the API rejects it with the documented error and the p95 latency of concurrent well-formed requests is unaffected

Scenario: Degradation ladder behaves as specified
  Given the WS gateway is driven into the saturated state
  Then profile topics are throttled to 1000 ms, a system notice is emitted, degraded_topics names the profile topic, and no sequence gap is introduced

Scenario: Budget regression fails CI
  Given a change that pushes 5 000-row p95 frame time beyond perf/budgets/e19.yaml
  When the benchmark job runs
  Then CI fails and names the violated budget

Scenario: Edge case - re-bucket under peak load
  Given a live session profile receiving peak-rate prints
  When the row size is changed
  Then the worker re-buckets within 300 ms and no print is lost or double counted across the switch
```

## Technical notes / design
- Benchmarks replay a recorded tape at a controlled rate so runs are comparable; injector lag is asserted and a run whose injector falls behind is invalidated rather than reported as a result.
- Reporting uses percentiles and run-to-run variance, never a single best run; minimum three runs per configuration.
- The GPU matrix reuses the machines named in the E11/E06 engine baseline so E19 numbers are directly comparable with the engine's own budgets in `26-chart-engine-design.md`.
- Composite queries are measured cold (page cache dropped) and warm, and both are reported - a warm-only number would hide the Parquet read cost that the 2 s budget exists to bound.
- WS coalescing correctness is validated by comparing the last coalesced frame against the oracle-computed profile at that timestamp, reusing `E19-Q02` fixtures rather than trusting the server's own view.

## Test plan
- Nightly: engine and compute benchmarks on the fixed hardware matrix, results pushed to the trend dashboard.
- Pre-merge: a fast subset (2 000 rows, one mode, one DPR) as a required check on profile paths.
- Pre-R2-exit: the full pack executed once and the report merged - this is the evidence for the R2 performance gate.

## Security notes
- Load scripts refuse any target host not on the allow-list, so accidental production load is structurally prevented.
- Test principals hold `marketdata:read` only; load credentials are short-lived, injected from CI secrets and never committed.
- The oversized-window scenario doubles as a denial-of-service resilience check; any finding is handed to `E19-X02` rather than only recorded as a performance note.

## Accessibility notes
- One configuration is measured with the `SCR-038` table alternative active and a screen reader attached, proving the DOM mirror for up to 5 000 rows does not itself blow the frame budget - virtualisation must be in effect.
- Reduced-motion mode is measured separately so the accessible path is never the slow path.

## Performance notes
- Budgets enforced: 24 h rebuild <= 1 s; visible-range recompute <= 10 Hz with pan-end debounce and >= 55 fps; 30-session composite <= 2 s cold tier; re-bucket <= 300 ms; 5 000 rows renderable; WS cadence 1 000 ms with the documented degradation behaviour.
- Any accepted deviation requires an owner-signed entry in the report plus a follow-up ticket; editing a budget without that trail is forbidden and reviewers are instructed to reject it.

## Observability
- Runs export `profile_rebuild_duration_seconds`, `profile_rows_total`, WS coalesce counters and queue depth, with Grafana snapshots attached to the report.
- Every scenario records commit sha, hardware id and tape id so a number remains reproducible months later.

## Definition of Done
- Scripts and `perf/budgets/e19.yaml` merged; nightly job green; fast subset wired as a required check.
- `docs/perf/e19-profiles-report.md` merged with measured numbers, a verdict per budget, and sign-off from the architect and the order-flow lead.
- A deliberately seeded regression demonstrated to fail the CI budget check.
- Every budget miss has either a filed ticket or a recorded accepted risk with the owner named.

## Dependencies
- `E19-T04` (engine profile plugin, LOD merging), `E19-T03` (WS topic and degradation), `E19-Q02` (oracle for coalescing correctness).
- E17 WS gateway backpressure machinery; E11/E06 benchmark harness and hardware matrix; E16 recorded tapes.

`test/e19-profile-perf`

- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` (LOD, instancing, DPR)

title: Chaos scenarios: feed gaps, store outages, recorder limits and restart recovery
body:
## Context
A profile is a *cumulative* structure: unlike a bar, it never re-derives itself from scratch during normal operation, so any lost, duplicated or out-of-order print silently deforms it for the rest of the period, and the deformation is invisible - the histogram still looks plausible. The planning brief makes chaos and failover testing (WS disconnect, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018) non-negotiable, and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 5 specifies the recovery design (5 s flush to QuestDB, rebuild on restart, top-up from trades, invalidation on `metadata_version` bump). That design must be *proven*, not assumed.

This ticket injects the realistic failures of a self-hosted stack - upstream WS drops, Bybit 5xx and rate limits, QuestDB and Parquet/DuckDB unavailability, disk pressure from retention, clock skew and process restarts - and asserts the profile either stays exactly correct or degrades visibly and honestly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/chaos/e19/` scenario pack, each scenario scripted, repeatable and asserted against the `E19-Q02` oracle:
  1. **Upstream WS disconnect mid-session** - drop the exchange trade stream for 30 s and restore; assert the gap is backfilled from REST or explicitly marked, and the final profile equals the uninterrupted oracle run or carries an explicit partial marker.
  2. **Duplicate and out-of-order prints on reconnect** - replay overlapping trade ids; assert idempotent accumulation with no double counting.
  3. **Exchange 5xx and rate-limit 10018 during backfill** - assert bounded retry with backoff, no partial double-application, and a user-visible "partial history" state rather than a wrong-but-confident profile.
  4. **QuestDB unavailable** - during flush and during rebuild; assert the in-RAM period survives a transient outage, that flushes resume without gaps, and that a rebuild attempted during an outage fails loudly with a named error state on `SCR-038`.
  5. **Cold tier (Parquet/DuckDB) unavailable** - composite request degrades to the hot-tier-covered range with the covered range stated, never a silently truncated composite.
  6. **Process restart at hostile moments** - immediately before a flush, mid-flush, and mid-rebuild; assert recovery equals the uninterrupted run.
  7. **Recorder limits and retention eviction** - the requested window extends before `recording_started_at`, or retention evicts data mid-session; assert the "History starts <ts>" empty/partial states and the approximated-from-bars path with the `EstimatedBadge`.
  8. **Clock skew and DST-free anchoring** - server clock steps forward and backward; assert UTC-anchored session boundaries and `funding_8h` anchors do not shift and no period is duplicated or lost.
  9. **WS client-side chaos** - client suspend/resume (laptop sleep), sequence gap, forced resubscribe; assert snapshot+delta re-sync per `23-ws-protocol.md` section 7 leaves the client profile identical to the server's.
  10. **`metadata_version` bump (tick size change) under load** - assert invalidation, rebuild scheduling and no mixed-grid rows served in the interim.
- Each scenario documents: injection method, expected system behaviour, expected user-visible state, and the assertion used (oracle equality, explicit marker, or named error).
- Results recorded in `docs/qa/e19-chaos-results.md` with a verdict per scenario.

## Out of scope
- Chaos for the ingestion layer itself (E16/E13) beyond its effect on profiles; this pack consumes those fault-injection hooks rather than building new ones.
- Order/OMS failover (E45) - no trading surface is involved in R2 profiles.
- Sustained multi-hour soak (E46).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A 30-second feed gap never produces a silently wrong profile
  Given the exchange trade stream drops for 30 seconds mid-session
  When the stream is restored and the gap is backfilled
  Then the resulting profile equals the oracle profile for the full session
  Or the profile is explicitly marked partial for that window with the gap stated

Scenario: Reconnect duplicates are idempotent
  Given the reconnect replays 5 000 trades already accumulated
  When accumulation continues
  Then total volume, per-row volumes and the POC are unchanged from the oracle

Scenario: Failure case - store outage fails loudly
  Given QuestDB is unavailable when a rebuild is requested
  When the user opens SCR-038
  Then a named error state with a retry action is shown and no empty profile is presented as a real one

Scenario: Edge case - restart mid-flush
  Given the process is killed while a 5 second flush is in progress
  When it restarts and tops up from raw trades
  Then the profile equals the uninterrupted run with no duplicated or missing rows

Scenario: Edge case - requested window predates recording
  Given a composite request reaching before recording_started_at
  Then the covered range is stated explicitly, the uncovered portion is either omitted with a partial chip or approximated from bars with the EstimatedBadge, and the POC is computed only over stated data

Scenario: Clock step does not move session boundaries
  Given the server clock steps back 2 seconds and later forward 5 seconds
  Then UTC-anchored and funding_8h session boundaries are unchanged and no period is duplicated or dropped
```

## Technical notes / design
- Injection uses the existing test proxy and container-level controls (pause the QuestDB container, blackhole the cold-tier mount, kill -9 the engine) so scenarios are reproducible in CI and on a developer machine.
- Every scenario ends with the same terminal assertion - oracle equality or an explicit honest marker - which keeps the pack from degenerating into "it did not crash".
- Backfill idempotency is asserted at the trade-id level, because duplicate suppression is the single mechanism protecting every cumulative surface in the product (profiles, footprint, CVD).
- Partial-state semantics are asserted against the exact `SCR-038` copy ("Partial: only N of M requested days recorded", "History starts <ts>") so the UX contract and the backend degrade in step.

## Test plan
- Run nightly in CI against a compose stack, plus once manually before the R2 gate on the staging host, since some faults (disk pressure) are only realistic there.
- Each scenario runs three times; a scenario that passes only sometimes is a failure and gets a bug, not a retry.
- Results feed the R2 exit review alongside `E19-Q04`.

## Security notes
- Fault injection tooling is confined to non-production environments by an allow-list guard; the pack refuses to run against a host without a `staging` or `local` marker.
- The pack includes one negative check that error states never leak internal details (stack traces, store hostnames, SQL) to the browser, per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.
- Retention-eviction scenarios confirm evicted data is genuinely unreadable afterwards, which is a data-lifecycle (R15) as well as a correctness concern.

## Accessibility notes
- Every degraded state exercised here is asserted to be announced, not merely drawn: partial chips, error states and the approximated badge must be reachable by keyboard and exposed to assistive technology, per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- A profile that silently empties is treated as a defect for screen-reader users specifically, since the visual absence of bars carries no announcement.

## Performance notes
- Recovery-time budgets are asserted: rebuild after restart completes within the same <= 1 s budget as a normal 24 h rebuild, and resubscribe re-sync delivers a usable snapshot within the WS reconnect budget from `23-ws-protocol.md`.
- Backfill after a gap must not starve live accumulation; the pack asserts live cadence is maintained during backfill.

## Observability
- Each scenario asserts the expected log events and metric movements (gap detected, backfill started/completed, flush failure, rebuild scheduled, invalidation on `metadata_version`), so operators can diagnose the same fault in production from telemetry alone.
- Missing telemetry for an injected fault is itself a scenario failure, not a nice-to-have.

## Definition of Done
- Scenario pack merged, nightly job green, `docs/qa/e19-chaos-results.md` published with a verdict per scenario.
- Every scenario has an automated assertion; none rely on manual observation.
- Defects found are filed with reproduction scripts referenced from this ticket.
- Reviewed by the order-flow lead, the SDET and DevSecOps (for the injection tooling guard-rails).

## Dependencies

title: Fixed-range, visible-range and anchored profiles with throttled recompute
body:
## Context
Implements **US-VP-002 — Fixed-range, visible-range and anchored profiles (Must/Should)**. A session profile answers one question; these three answer every other one — "what happened in *this* move", "what does the current view say", "what has accumulated since *that* bar". The roadmap lists "profile anchoring to drawings and to sessions" in the E19 scope line, so the anchored mode binds to a chart anchor rather than a fixed timestamp typed into a dialog. The hard constraint is performance: "visible-range recompute throttled to ≤10 Hz with a debounce on pan end" and "interaction stays at ≥55 fps".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Fixed range**: drag a range selection on the time axis → a profile pinned to exactly those timestamps, surviving pan, zoom, reload and interval change (`ProfilePeriod.kind = fixed_range`).
- **Visible range**: recomputes as the viewport changes, throttled to ≤10 Hz with a debounce on pan/zoom end; a stale-while-recomputing state rather than a blank pane.
- **Anchored**: anchor at a bar (or at an existing drawing's anchor, per the roadmap's "anchoring to drawings") and accumulate forward indefinitely; the anchor is a `{t}` in chart space, invariant across bar-type and scale changes exactly as drawing anchors are.
- Range handles: move and resize a fixed range from the chart; the range and its duration shown in the legend.
- Bootstrap/streaming: fixed and anchored periods stream live via WS when their end is open; visible-range recompute is worker-local from cached raw data, falling back to a REST fetch only when the viewport leaves the cached window.
- Multiple concurrent profile instances per pane, each with its own period, respecting the per-connection subscription cap from **E19-T03**.

## Out of scope
- Composite/multi-session periods (**E19-S03**) and the settings dialog (**E19-S09**).
- Swing-anchored auto-detection (SCR-039 lists "Swing-anchored" as a period type; automatic swing detection is **E25** — this story supports a manual anchor only).
- Replay-time period behaviour — **E26**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fixed range
  When I drag a range selection
  Then a profile is computed for exactly that window and stays pinned to those timestamps

Scenario: Visible range
  Given visible-range mode
  Then the profile recomputes as I pan and zoom, throttled so interaction stays at >= 55 fps

Scenario: Anchored
  When I anchor at a specific bar
  Then the profile accumulates forward from that bar and can be extended indefinitely

Scenario: Anchors survive a bar-type change
  Given an anchored profile on 1m time bars
  When the chart switches to 500-tick bars and back
  Then the anchor resolves to the same timestamp and the accumulated profile is unchanged

Scenario: Viewport leaves the cached window
  Given the visible range is panned beyond the cached raw histogram
  Then a bounded REST fetch tops up the cache, the pane shows a recomputing state, and interaction is not blocked

Scenario: Degenerate range
  When a range selection is shorter than one bar or has zero duration
  Then no period is created and the selection is cancelled with a hint
```

## Technical notes / design
All three modes are the same `ProfilePeriod` with different `kind`/bounds, so the engine and renderer need no new code paths — this story is period lifecycle plus interaction. Visible-range is deliberately client-side: a server round-trip per pan frame is exactly the real-time-cost risk (R3) the WS backpressure ladder exists to avoid, so the worker re-aggregates its cached raw histogram and the server is consulted only on a cache miss. Throttling uses a leading-edge 10 Hz gate plus a trailing debounce on pan end, so the user sees motion immediately and an exact result when they stop.

## Test plan
Unit: period construction per mode, range-handle maths, throttle/debounce gate, cache-miss detection. Property-based: anchored period anchor `(t)` invariant across random bar specs and scale modes (the same property E14 uses for drawing anchors). E2E: drag-create a fixed range and reload; visible-range pan with an fps assertion; anchor and extend. Perf: pan/zoom in visible-range mode sustains ≥55 fps with a 5 000-row profile; recompute rate measured ≤10 Hz.

## Security notes
Each concurrent period is a server-side resource: the per-pane instance count and the per-connection subscription cap from T03 are enforced server-side, so a scripted client cannot open unbounded periods. Cache top-up requests use the same bounded parameters as T02.

## Accessibility notes
Range selection has a keyboard path: the range can be created and resized from the keyboard by stepping bar-by-bar with `Enter` to confirm, mirroring the E14 keyboard drawing pattern; the selected range's start, end and duration are announced. Mode selection is a labelled radio group (SCR-039 pattern). The recomputing state is announced politely, not as an alert.

## Performance notes
≤10 Hz recompute with a pan-end debounce; ≥55 fps sustained; worker re-aggregation ≤ 8 ms at p95 per the R4 budget; cache top-up bounded and asynchronous.

## Observability
`profile_visible_range_recompute_ms`, `profile_cache_miss_total`, `profile_active_periods{period_kind}`; analytics `profile.period_changed{kind}`, `profile.range_created`, `profile.anchor_set`.

- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests; anchor-invariance property test ≥10k cases.
- [ ] fps and recompute-rate assertions recorded in the perf report.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend; axe-core green; keyboard range creation verified with a screen reader.
- [ ] design-qa sign-off; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E19-S01**. Blocks **E19-S03**, **E19-S09**.

## Branch
`feat/e19-range-anchored-profiles`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-VP-002; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §5.1 `ProfilePeriod`; `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 R4, §3.10 anchors, §15; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-038, SCR-039; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 E19.

title: HVN / LVN detection with configurable prominence and metric exposure
body:
## Context
Implements **US-VP-005 — HVN / LVN detection (Should)**. High- and low-volume nodes are where price accelerates or stalls; marking them turns the histogram from a picture into levels. The algorithm is already pinned in `24-internal-schemas.md` §5.2: centred moving-average smoothing over `smoothing_levels` (default 3), HVN = local maximum with raw volume ≥ `hvn_min_pct` (0.5) of POC volume, LVN = local minimum with raw volume ≤ `lvn_max_pct` (0.25) of POC volume, adjacent peaks within `merge_ticks` (default `3 * aggregation_ticks`) merged into the higher. The story's NFR: "detection is deterministic and unit-tested against fixture profiles."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Detection in `ProfileEngine` per §5.2, populating `hvn_ticks` / `lvn_ticks`; served through `include_hvn_lvn` on `GET /market/profile` and the `hvn`/`lvn` arrays of `ProfileUpdate`.
- Sensitivity controls in **SCR-039**: `smoothing_levels`, `hvn_min_pct`, `lvn_max_pct`, `merge_ticks` — raising the threshold yields fewer, more significant nodes.
- Rendering: node markers with labels through the T04 plugin's flags; single-print/LVN highlighting toggle (SCR-038 shows LVN and single prints marked with `*`).
- Metric exposure: HVN/LVN price levels published on the internal metric bus under stable names for **E40** alerts and **E35** rules (US-VP-005 scenario "Exposure").

## Out of scope
- Alert creation on node touches — **E40**.
- Naked POC (**E19-S06**) and TPO single prints as a *TPO* concept (**E19-S08**; this story handles volume-histogram single prints only).
- Automatic node-based support/resistance scoring — not in R2.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Detection
  Then peaks and valleys are marked using the configured prominence threshold, with labels

Scenario: Sensitivity
  When I increase the threshold
  Then fewer, more significant nodes are marked

Scenario: Exposure
  Then HVN/LVN price levels are available as metrics and can trigger alerts

Scenario: Deterministic on a fixture
  Given the committed fixture profiles
  When detection runs repeatedly and on different nodes
  Then the same node sets are produced every time, byte for byte

Scenario: Adjacent peaks merge
  Given two local maxima within merge_ticks of each other
  Then they are reported as one node at the higher of the two, not two adjacent nodes

Scenario: Flat or empty histogram
  Given a period with a single traded level or no trades at all
  Then no nodes are reported and no error is raised
```

## Technical notes / design
Smoothing is applied for **detection only**; the reported node volume is the raw level's, so a node's label never disagrees with the row the user hovers. Detection runs on the same worker/engine pass as POC/VA so a settings change recomputes all three together. Defaults are chosen to be conservative — over-marking is the common failure mode of node detection and makes the feature useless — and the fixture suite includes a deliberately noisy profile to guard against regression toward over-marking.

## Test plan
Unit (≥85%): smoothing, local-extremum detection, threshold filters, merge rule, degenerate histograms. Golden data: committed fixture profiles with expected node sets, asserted exactly. Property-based: raising `hvn_min_pct` never increases the HVN count (monotonicity). E2E: sensitivity change reduces marks; metric names appear on the metric bus. Visual: golden images with node markers in both themes.

## Security notes
Sensitivity parameters are numeric and bounded server-side; no new endpoint. Metrics are read-only market data under `marketdata:read`.

## Accessibility notes
Nodes are marked with a glyph and a text label ("HVN 63,020"), never colour alone, and appear as a flagged column in the table alternative so a screen-reader user gets the same level list. Sensitivity controls are labelled with units and their effect described in the field help ("higher = fewer, more significant nodes").

## Performance notes
Detection is O(levels) over an already-materialised histogram and runs inside the existing POC/VA pass — no measurable addition to the ≤ 8 ms viewport budget; measured in the B-profile benchmark with detection enabled.

## Observability
`profile_node_detection_duration_ms`, `profile_nodes_detected{type=hvn|lvn}`; analytics `profile.node_sensitivity_changed`, `profile.nodes_toggled`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests; fixture node sets asserted exactly.
- [ ] Monotonicity property test green.
- [ ] Metric names published and referenced by the E40 backlog item.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% engine; axe-core green; design-qa sign-off; demoed.

## Dependencies

title: Naked / virgin POC tracking with server-side tested state and clutter limit
body:
## Context
Implements **US-VP-006 — Naked / virgin POC tracking (Should)**: prior sessions' POCs carried forward as targets until price trades through them. The NFR is unusual and drives the design: "state maintained **server-side** so it is consistent across panes and users." `24-internal-schemas.md` §5.2 specifies the lifecycle: maintained incrementally, on every bar close any naked POC inside the bar's `[low, high]` flips to `tested` with `tested_at`; retained for `naked_poc_lookback_periods` (default 20); rendered as horizontal rays. The `naked_poc` boolean already exists in both the REST `ProfileResponse` and the WS `ProfileUpdate`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Server-side naked-POC registry per `(env, symbol)`: prior-period POCs with `tested`/`tested_at`, updated on every bar close, rebuilt deterministically from recorded history on restart.
- Retention: `naked_poc_lookback_periods` (default 20) and a **clutter limit** — only the nearest N to current price are drawn (configurable), with an explicit count of hidden ones (US-VP-006 scenario "Limit clutter").
- Rendering: horizontal rays from the originating session forward to current price; tested POCs visually **demoted** rather than deleted, with a history toggle.
- Exposure: `naked_poc` on profile payloads plus naked-POC levels on the metric bus for **E40**/**E35**.
- Backfill: on first enablement for a symbol, naked POCs are computed from recorded sessions within the look-back and the covered range is stated where history is short.

## Out of scope
- Alerting on a naked-POC touch — **E40** consumes the exposed levels.
- Naked VAH/VAL and other untested-level families — not in R2.
- Cross-symbol or higher-timeframe composite naked POCs.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Carry forward
  Then each prior session's POC is drawn as a level until price trades through it

Scenario: Flip on retest
  When price trades through a naked POC
  Then it is marked tested and visually demoted, retaining a history toggle

Scenario: Limit clutter
  Given more than N naked POCs exist
  Then only the nearest N to current price are drawn, configurable, with a count of hidden ones

Scenario: State is shared, not per-pane
  Given two panes and two users viewing the same symbol
  Then both see the identical naked/tested state at the same instant

Scenario: Restart is deterministic
  Given the service restarts
  When the registry is rebuilt from recorded history
  Then the naked/tested state is identical to the pre-restart state

Scenario: History too short to back-fill
  Given the recorder covers fewer sessions than the look-back
  Then naked POCs are computed from what exists and the covered range is stated explicitly
```

## Technical notes / design
Server-side state is the whole point: a client-side implementation would drift between panes and between users, and the level would "untest" itself on reload. The registry is a small per-symbol structure persisted alongside profile flushes, and the flip check is O(naked count) per bar close — trivial. A POC is tested when a bar's `[low, high]` **covers** it, not merely when a trade prints at it, matching the textbook definition and the §5.2 wording. Clutter limiting is a render-time selection over the full server-side set, so raising N reveals existing levels instantly without a refetch.

## Test plan
Unit (≥85%): flip rule incl. exact-touch boundary (bar low == POC), look-back eviction, nearest-N selection, hidden count. Integration: multi-session fixture with a POC tested three sessions later; restart rebuild equality; short-history backfill. E2E: two panes observe the same flip; history toggle. Visual: golden images of naked vs tested rays, both themes.

## Security notes
Shared server-side state is read-only market data with no per-user component, so there is no cross-user leakage concern; it is exposed under `marketdata:read` like every other `/market/*` surface. The registry is bounded by `naked_poc_lookback_periods` per symbol, so it cannot grow without limit.

## Accessibility notes
Naked and tested rays differ in line style and carry text labels ("naked POC 63,020" / "POC 62,410 — tested 2026-09-12"), not colour alone. The hidden-count is text ("4 more naked POCs above"), and the table alternative lists every naked POC with its state and origin session. The history toggle is a labelled switch.

## Performance notes
O(naked count) per bar close (≤20 by default); render cost is a handful of lines within the existing ≤3 text draw-call budget; no additional network traffic (levels ride on the existing profile payload).

## Observability
`profile_naked_poc_count{symbol}`, `profile_naked_poc_flips_total`, `profile_naked_registry_rebuild_duration_ms`; analytics `profile.naked_poc_toggled`, `profile.naked_poc_limit_changed`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Restart-determinism test green.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% engine / ≥80% frontend; axe-core green; design-qa sign-off; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E19-S05** (shares the level-marking render path and the metric-exposure pattern); transitively **E19-S04** for POC. Blocks nothing in E19; consumed by **E40**.

## Branch
`feat/e19-naked-poc`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-VP-006; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §5.2 naked/virgin POC; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `naked_poc`; `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §14.6; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-039.

title: Abuse cases: parameter fuzzing, exhaustion and profile integrity
body:
## Context
`E19-X01` rates the threats; this ticket tries to realise them. The profile read surface is the widest parameter surface in R2 - `symbol`, `kind`, `from`, `to`, `split`, `session_anchor`, `session_anchor_time`, `fixed_duration_minutes`, `price_grouping`, `value_area_pct`, `tpo_period_minutes`, `include_hvn_lvn` - sitting in front of a hot store and an expensive cold tier, plus a WS topic whose key includes several of the same parameters. Two attack classes matter: **resource exhaustion** (legal-looking requests that cost far more than they appear to) and **integrity** (making the published POC/VAH/VAL differ from reality, since those values arm rules).

`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires abuse-case testing per epic alongside SAST/DAST, and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires those tests to be automated where possible so they keep running.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Parameter fuzzing suite** `security/abuse/e19/` against `GET /api/v1/market/profile`:
  - Type and range violations for every parameter (negative, zero, non-numeric, overflowing integers, `value_area_pct` at 49.9/50/95/95.1, `price_grouping` 0/1/1000/1001, `tpo_period_minutes` 0/1/240/241, malformed `session_anchor_time`, `from > to`, identical `from`/`to`, far-future and epoch-zero timestamps).
  - Symbol-field injection attempts (SQL-ish payloads, path traversal, null bytes, unicode homoglyphs, extremely long strings) verifying parameterised queries and strict symbol validation against the instrument registry - never a pass-through to QuestDB or DuckDB.
  - Content-type, header and encoding abuse (oversized query strings, duplicated parameters with conflicting values, parameter pollution) asserting deterministic, documented resolution rather than last-wins surprises.
  - Assertion for every case: a documented `400`/`422` error from the catalogue with no stack trace, no SQL fragment, no file path, no store hostname, and no unbounded work performed before rejection.
- **Resource-exhaustion scenarios**:
  - Maximum-cost legal request (30-session composite, `price_grouping=1`, `tpo_period_minutes=1`, `include_hvn_lvn=true`) issued concurrently; assert bounded-window/row-cap rejection or an enforced cost ceiling, and that well-formed traffic keeps its p95 latency.
  - Rapid-fire visible-range recompute simulating a scripted client ignoring client-side throttling; assert server-side rate limiting, not reliance on the browser.
  - WS subscription flood: one principal subscribing to many `profile.{symbol}.{kind}` permutations (all kinds x all splits x many symbols); assert per-connection and per-principal subscription quotas, and that the degradation ladder engages before the gateway is harmed.
  - Slow-consumer attack: subscribe and stop reading; assert backpressure and disconnection per `23-ws-protocol.md` section 8 rather than unbounded server-side buffering.
- **Integrity abuse cases**:
  - Replayed/duplicated trade ids injected via the test feed; assert idempotent accumulation leaves POC/VA unchanged.
  - Out-of-order and far-future-timestamped prints; assert they are clamped or rejected, never silently placed in the wrong period.
  - Direct out-of-band mutation of a QuestDB profiles row followed by a served request; assert either detection or that a forced rebuild from raw trades restores truth, and document which guarantee actually holds.
  - Tick-size (`metadata_version`) flapping during heavy load; assert invalidation is atomic and no mixed-grid profile is ever served.
- **Authorization cases**: a principal without `marketdata:read` on REST and WS; a principal attempting a symbol outside its allowed list; token expiry mid-subscription asserting revocation per `23-ws-protocol.md` section 9; IDOR-style attempts to read another user's saved profile presets.
- Findings logged with severity, reproduction and a fix owner; high findings block `E19-X04`.

## Out of scope
- Network and host hardening (E03/E43) and exchange-side key abuse (E27/E28).
- Full pen-test - this is the epic-level precursor whose findings scope the R4 pen-test.
- Functional correctness with valid inputs (`E19-Q02`) and budget measurement (`E19-Q04`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every invalid parameter is rejected cleanly
  Given the fuzzing corpus for GET /api/v1/market/profile
  When each request is sent
  Then the response is a documented 400 or 422 with no stack trace, SQL fragment, file path or internal hostname
  And no request performs a store query before validation rejects it

Scenario: Symbol input cannot reach the data stores
  Given injection payloads in the symbol parameter
  Then every request is rejected by instrument-registry validation and no query containing the payload appears in QuestDB or DuckDB logs

Scenario: Failure case - maximum-cost legal requests cannot starve the service
  Given 50 concurrent 30-session composites at price_grouping=1
  Then the cost ceiling or bounded-window limit rejects or queues them, and the p95 latency of concurrent well-formed requests stays within budget

Scenario: Subscription flood is bounded
  Given one principal subscribing to every kind and split across 200 symbols
  Then per-principal subscription quotas reject the excess with a documented error and the gateway stays healthy for other clients

Scenario: Edge case - duplicate prints cannot move the POC
  Given 5 000 already-accumulated trades replayed into the engine
  Then total volume, row volumes and the POC are unchanged

Scenario: Authorization is enforced on both transports
  Given a principal lacking marketdata:read
  Then both the REST endpoint and the WS subscription are refused with the documented error, and no profile data is returned on either path

Scenario: Revocation takes effect on a live subscription
  Given an active profile subscription whose token is revoked
  Then the server terminates or downgrades the subscription per the protocol and stops sending profile frames
```

## Technical notes / design
- The fuzzing corpus is generated from the OpenAPI parameter definitions so it stays in step with the contract automatically; a new parameter with no corpus entry fails the suite, which prevents the corpus from silently aging.
- Exhaustion scenarios assert *cost control*, not just eventual completion: the pass condition is that expensive requests are bounded or rejected, because "it finished in 40 seconds" is a successful attack on a single-tenant self-hosted box.
- The out-of-band store mutation case is deliberately included even though the store is inside the trust boundary, because the honest outcome is a documented statement of which integrity guarantee exists - detection, rebuild-on-demand, or none - and the product should not pretend to a guarantee it lacks.
- Slow-consumer behaviour is asserted against the documented backpressure ladder rather than against memory growth alone, so the test survives tuning changes.

## Test plan
- Suite runs nightly against staging and pre-merge in a reduced form on PRs touching the profile API or WS routing.
- Each finding gets a permanent regression case so a fixed issue cannot silently return.
- Results feed `E19-X04` and the R2 exit gate via `E19-Q08`.

## Security notes
- Execution is restricted to staging and local environments by an allow-list guard in the harness; running the exhaustion scenarios against production is prevented, not merely discouraged.
- Credentials for negative-authorization cases are short-lived, provisioned by the test harness, and never committed.
- Findings follow the `04-security-program.md` severity scale and disclosure process; high findings are tracked privately until fixed rather than in public issue text.
- Any information-disclosure finding (error text leaking internals) is fixed centrally in the error catalogue so sibling endpoints inherit the fix.

## Accessibility notes
- Error and rate-limit states triggered by these cases must render as announced, keyboard-reachable states on `SCR-038` rather than as silent failures; the suite includes one UI-level check per class (validation error, rate limited, unauthorized) confirming the state exists and is exposed to assistive technology.

## Performance notes
- Exhaustion scenarios reuse the `E19-Q04` harness and budgets so security limits and performance budgets are validated against the same numbers.
- The suite records the marginal cost of the most expensive legal request, which is the input to setting the documented cost ceiling.

## Observability
- Every abuse scenario asserts that the corresponding telemetry fires (rejected-window counter, rate-limit counter, subscription-quota rejections, authorization failures), proving the detection list from `E19-X01` is real.
- Missing telemetry is itself a finding, since an undetectable attack is an unmitigated one.

## Definition of Done
- Suite merged and running nightly; reduced form wired as a required check on profile API/WS paths.
- All findings triaged: high fixed or Owner-accepted, medium/low with owners and target trains.
- Regression cases added for each finding; the detection assertions green.
- Reviewed by the Security engineer and the order-flow lead; results linked from `E19-X01` and `E19-X04`.

## Dependencies
- `E19-X01` (threat model and abuse-case seed list), `E19-T02` (bounded windows), `E19-T03` (WS topic, quotas, degradation).
- E09 RBAC scopes, E17 WS authorization and revocation, `E19-Q04` load harness.

- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/profile` parameters and error responses

title: ADR and reference doc for profile period semantics, value area and naked POC
body:
## Context
E19 settles several decisions that are not obvious, are contested among traders, and will be depended upon by alerts (E40), the rule engine, backtesting (R4) and any future mobile client: how a "session" is defined for a 24/7 market, which value-area expansion algorithm is used, how POC ties break, how TPO periods and letters are assigned, when a POC counts as naked, and what the approximated-from-bars fallback means numerically. Today these live scattered across `22-api-openapi.yaml` prose, `24-internal-schemas.md` section 5 and the test plan.

`docs/plan/27-adrs/` is where decisions with downstream consequences are recorded, and the epic DoD requires the plan docs to reflect shipped behaviour rather than the original proposal. Without this, a future engineer will "fix" the single-step expansion to the textbook algorithm and silently change where every rule arms.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Surfaces documented: SCR-038 profile panel, SCR-039 settings dialog; components CMP-110 ProfileBar, CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane, CMP-184 MarketProfileTpoPane.
- **ADR** `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-00XX-profile-period-and-value-area-semantics.md` (number assigned at authoring time) covering:
  - Session definition for crypto: UTC-day default, `funding_8h` and `custom` anchors, and why no RTH concept is used.
  - Value-area algorithm: single-step expansion toward the heavier adjacent row, stated as an explicit accepted approximation of two-row TPO expansion, with the consequences and the conditions under which it differs.
  - POC tie-break: closest to range midpoint, deterministic, surfaced in the tooltip.
  - TPO period and letter assignment: default 30 minutes, configurable 1..240, letters `A..Z, a..z, AA..`, initial-balance period count.
  - Naked/virgin POC definition: when a POC becomes naked, what counts as "traded through", server-side state, and the nearest-N display cap.
  - HVN/LVN prominence definition and default threshold.
  - Approximated-from-bars fallback: exactly what is derived from klines, what is not available (delta, TPO), and how it is labelled.
  - Decimal/float boundary per `24-internal-schemas.md` C3 and which published values are exact.
  - Alternatives considered and rejected, with reasons, so the decisions are not relitigated from scratch.
- **Reference doc** `docs/plan/reference/profiles.md`: a single consumer-facing page for downstream epics listing each published metric (`profile_poc`, `profile_vah`, `profile_val`, HVN/LVN levels), its parameterisation, exactness, update cadence and failure modes (partial history, approximated, stale during rebuild).
- **Doc updates**: `24-internal-schemas.md` section 5 and the `/market/profile` description reconciled with shipped behaviour if they diverged; `18-traceability-matrix.md` section 2.9 refreshed if coverage changed.
- Cross-links added from the E40 alerts and rule-engine epics so consumers find the guarantees before designing against them.

## Out of scope
- Changing any of the algorithms - this records what shipped; a change requires a new ticket and a superseding ADR.
- End-user help content and tooltips (product copy owned by design), though the ADR supplies the factual basis and the known-limitations wording from `E19-Q08` is reused.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every contested decision is recorded with a rationale
  Given the merged ADR
  When it is reviewed against the E19 implementation
  Then session anchoring, value-area expansion, POC tie-break, TPO letters, naked POC, HVN/LVN and the bar-approximation fallback each have a decision, a rationale and the alternatives rejected

Scenario: Documentation matches shipped behaviour
  Given the shipped release-candidate build
  When 24-internal-schemas.md section 5 and the /market/profile description are compared to it
  Then any divergence is corrected in the docs, and the ADR states the correction

Scenario: Failure case - an undocumented behavioural difference is found
  Given the implementation breaks a tie differently from the documented rule
  Then the discrepancy is filed as a correctness bug against the owning ticket and the ADR is not merged claiming a rule that the code does not follow

Scenario: Downstream consumers can rely on the reference page
  Given the reference doc
  When an E40 alerts engineer needs to know whether profile_vah is exact and how often it updates
  Then the page answers both without reading engine source

Scenario: ADR is approved
  When the ADR PR is opened
  Then the Architect, the order-flow lead and the Security engineer approve it and it is linked from the E19 epic
```

## Technical notes / design
- The ADR is written as a decision record, not a tutorial: context, decision, consequences, alternatives. Tutorial-style explanation belongs in the reference page, which is aimed at a different reader.
- The single most important consequence to state plainly is that these definitions are now *contract*: changing any of them alters historical comparability and the behaviour of armed rules, and therefore requires a superseding ADR and a migration note, not a bug fix.
- The reference page lists failure modes alongside guarantees, because a consumer that does not know a metric can be stale during a rebuild will design an alert that fires on a transient.
- Numbers in both documents are taken from the `E19-Q02` verified fixtures, so the documentation and the tests cannot disagree.

## Test plan
- Documentation is validated against the conformance suite: each documented rule names the test that proves it, and a rule with no test is either tested or marked unverified explicitly.
- A link check and a reference check run in CI so the new files are wired into the plan docs rather than orphaned.

## Security notes
- The ADR records the integrity and auditability guarantees agreed in `E19-X04`, so the security posture is discoverable by consumers instead of living only in a sign-off document.
- It states the parameter-recording requirement for rule evaluations (repudiation mitigation from the threat model), making it a design input to E40 rather than a late discovery.
- No secrets, hostnames or internal topology are included; the documents are safe for the repository's normal audience.

## Accessibility notes
- The reference page follows the documentation accessibility conventions (proper heading hierarchy, tables with headers, no meaning conveyed by colour alone in diagrams), per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- Where profile concepts are illustrated, a text description accompanies any diagram so the page is usable with a screen reader.

## Performance notes
- The reference page records the update cadence and rebuild latency characteristics of each published metric, so consumers size their polling and alert evaluation appropriately rather than discovering the 1 000 ms cadence by experiment.

## Observability
- Documents the metric and log names emitted by the profile engine, so operators and future debuggers can find them without reading code.

## Definition of Done
- ADR merged with a status of Accepted and a number assigned; reference page merged and linked from `24-internal-schemas.md`, the epic and the consuming epics.
- Plan docs reconciled with shipped behaviour; any discrepancy found during writing filed as a bug and resolved.
- Approved by the Architect, the order-flow lead and the Security engineer.
- Link check green; `18-traceability-matrix.md` section 2.9 refreshed if needed.

## Dependencies
- `E19-Q02` (verified numbers and rules) and `E19-X04` (security guarantees to record).
- Consumed by E40 alerts, the rule engine and the R4 backtesting work.

`docs/e19-profile-semantics-adr`

- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 5 and section 12
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/profile`; `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 14.6
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 9

title: Design QA of the shipped profile panel, settings dialog and TPO pane
body:
## Context
Design QA is the closing gate of the design loop defined in `16-design-system-brief.md` §12: the built profile surface is compared against the signed-off pack from E19-D07, and divergences are logged, classified and driven to closure before E19 can reach Done. For a GPU-rendered surface this pass matters more than usual — subpixel row alignment, bar-length quantisation, letter legibility at small sizes and colour rendering on different GPUs are things that only appear in the real renderer, and `R8 Browser/GPU compat` is a live risk on this epic.

This runs in Sprint 13, after the E19 frontend stories land in Sprint 10–13, against a real build with real recorded data.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Side-by-side comparison of the shipped **SCR-038** (docked and overlay) and **SCR-039** against the E19-D07 pack, in dark and light themes, at all three density modes.
- Verification of every state enumerated in the catalogue: loading · partial history · no history (owner and non-owner variants) · approximated-from-bars · degraded feed · developing vs final value area.
- Verification of every mode combination: period (session / fixed range / visible range / anchored / composite) × input (volume / delta / TPO), including split bid/ask rendering and the TPO Initial Balance.
- Edge-density verification against real recorded data: 5 000 rows at minimum row size; a two-level profile on an illiquid symbol; a 30-session composite; a value area spanning the whole visible range; more naked POCs than the clutter cap.
- Derived-level verification: POC, VAH, VAL, HVN, LVN, naked POC and single prints each rendered with the specified non-colour encoding and text label; POC tie-break tooltip present and correct.
- Motion verification against the E19-D05 spec including the suppression matrix: reduced-motion, saturated connection class, high row count, replay fast-forward.
- Accessibility verification against E19-D06: keyboard traversal end to end, focus-visible at every stop, the table alternative present and faithful, the announcement policy behaving under a live tape (specifically: no per-print flooding), target sizes at compact density, axe-core results reviewed.
- Cross-GPU/browser spot check per `R8`: the profile and TPO panes rendered on at least two distinct GPU/driver combinations, checking colour rendering, line thickness and letter legibility.
- Findings log, each classified blocker / must-fix / should-fix / accepted, with an owning ticket; blockers and must-fixes closed and re-verified before sign-off.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of the profile computation itself (POC/value-area maths, composite merging) — that is the engineering stories' unit and integration tests, not design QA.
- Backend performance measurement — E19's perf tickets own that; design QA only reports where a perf problem manifests visually.
- New scope or design changes; anything that is a genuinely new requirement is raised as a separate ticket under change control, not smuggled in as a QA fix.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The build matches the signed-off pack
  When the shipped SCR-038 and SCR-039 are compared with the E19-D07 redlines in both themes and all densities
  Then every divergence is logged with a classification and an owning ticket

Scenario: No blocker or must-fix remains open at sign-off
  Given the findings log contains items classified blocker or must-fix
  Then each is closed and re-verified in a subsequent build before this ticket reaches Done

Scenario: Colour is still not the sole carrier in the real renderer
  Given the shipped panel rendered in greyscale and under all three colour-blindness simulations
  Then POC, value area, HVN, LVN, naked POC, single prints and the buy/sell split all remain identifiable

Scenario: A live profile does not flood the screen reader
  Given a live session profile on an active symbol with a fast tape
  When a screen reader is active for two minutes
  Then routine updates are not announced and only the changes named in the E19-D06 announcement policy are

Scenario: Extreme density degrades as designed
  Given a profile with 5 000 rows at the minimum row size
  Then the shipped bucketing matches the designed appearance, motion is suppressed per the matrix, and interaction remains at or above the 55 fps floor

Scenario: A GPU difference is caught, not shipped
  Given the panel is rendered on a second GPU or driver combination
  When colours, line weights and TPO letters are compared against the first
  Then any visible difference is logged, and a difference that changes meaning is classified at least must-fix
```

## Technical notes / design
QA is run against a build fed by recorded fixtures so the edge cases are reproducible: the same fixture set used in E19-D01 plus the illiquid-symbol and 30-session-composite fixtures. The degraded-feed state is produced by forcing the `saturated` connection class from `23-ws-protocol.md` §8.3 rather than by waiting for it to occur naturally. Replay (E26) is used to reproduce the fast-forward motion-suppression case deterministically.

Row alignment in docked mode is checked against the axis-alignment rule written in E19-D02 with the chart in both linear and log price scale, and during an auto-fit animation — misalignment here is a correctness-class defect, not a cosmetic one, and should be classified accordingly.

## Test plan
Structured pass, not exploratory-only: a checklist derived directly from the E19-D07 pack, the SCR-038/SCR-039 sign-off acceptance checklists in `14-screens-catalogue.md`, the §12 design QA checklist in `16-design-system-brief.md`, and the E19-D06 findings. Evidence is screenshots and short clips attached to each finding. Re-verification of closed findings is done against a named build, and the build identifier is recorded on the ticket.

## Security notes
QA is run against recorded market fixtures and, where a live environment is needed, against demo only — never against live credentials. No account identifiers, balances or keys appear in any attached screenshot or clip; screenshots are reviewed for incidental account chrome before attachment.

## Accessibility notes
The a11y portion of this pass is a build-time verification of the design-time decisions in E19-D06: axe-core results reviewed alongside a manual NVDA and VoiceOver pass, full keyboard-only traversal, the table alternative checked for faithfulness against the histogram, and target sizes measured at compact density. A manual screen-reader pass is required by the Epic DoD in `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 and this ticket is where it is recorded for E19's screens.

## Performance notes
Design QA records the observed frame rate during visible-range panning at the worst supported density and row count, and the observed re-bucket latency on a row-size change, and compares them to the budgets carried in the E19-D07 pack. Failures are routed to the owning engineering ticket rather than absorbed as design findings.

## Observability
The pass confirms `profile.period_changed`, `profile.mode_changed`, `profile.va_percent_changed` and `profile.settings_changed` are actually emitted with the payloads specified in the pack, since an event that was specified but never wired is a silent gap that only a QA pass catches.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Full QA pass completed against a named build with findings logged, classified and assigned.
- [ ] All blocker and must-fix findings closed and re-verified on a later named build.
- [ ] Manual screen-reader pass and axe-core review recorded for SCR-038 and SCR-039.
- [ ] Cross-GPU spot check completed on at least two GPU/driver combinations with results attached.
- [ ] Observed fps and re-bucket latency recorded against the stated budgets.
- [ ] SCR-038 and SCR-039 sign-off acceptance checklists in `14-screens-catalogue.md` verified against the build, not the design.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded on the ticket; Status = Done.**

## Dependencies
- **E19-D07** supplies the pack this pass compares against.
- The E19 frontend stories (Sprint 10–13) must be feature-complete for the surfaces under review.
- **E26** replay is used to reproduce the fast-forward motion-suppression case.

## Branch
`design/e19-profile-design-qa`

## References
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §12 design QA checklist, §13.5 change control
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-038, SCR-039 sign-off acceptance checklists
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 Epic DoD, §3.2 Story DoD
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §8.3
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-VP-001 … US-VP-009

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`
2. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`

title: Accessibility audit of the profile panel, table alternative and settings dialog
body:
## Context
A volume profile is the most colour-dependent surface in the product after the heatmap: POC, value area, HVN/LVN, delta sign and TPO single prints are all conventionally signalled by hue and fill alone. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI and manual screen-reader passes, and `SCR-038` commits to a specific remedy - a table alternative listing each price row with volume, delta and value-area membership, with POC/VAH/VAL announced. That commitment needs auditing against a real build, because a 5 000-row DOM mirror is easy to implement in a way that is technically present and practically unusable.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Full manual and automated audit of `SCR-038` (profile panel, including the docked-beside-chart and overlay presentations) and `SCR-039` (settings dialog), covering CMP-110 ProfileBar, CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane, CMP-184 MarketProfileTpoPane, CMP-188 PriceAxis, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, CMP-228 PreviewTile and the `SCR-039` form controls (CMP-006, CMP-008, CMP-031, CMP-040, CMP-043, CMP-065).
- **Automated**: axe-core runs across every state - loading, populated, partial history, no history, approximated-from-bars, error - in volume, delta, TPO and combined modes, light and dark themes, at 200% and 400% zoom and at 320 px reflow width.
- **Manual screen-reader passes**: NVDA + Firefox, JAWS + Chrome, VoiceOver + Safari. Scripted tasks: find the POC price; determine whether the current price is inside the value area; read the three highest-volume rows; change the value-area percentage to 68; identify a naked POC; switch to TPO and find the initial balance.
- **Keyboard-only pass**: reach the panel, traverse rows, jump to POC/VAH/VAL, open and dismiss `SCR-039` with focus return, operate every control including the numeric steppers and colour swatches, with a visible focus indicator throughout and no keyboard trap.
- **Non-colour encoding review**: POC, value-area membership, delta sign, HVN/LVN and single prints each verified to carry a text, pattern, border or glyph affordance in addition to colour; verified under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia simulation and in the high-contrast theme.
- **Contrast measurements** for bar fills against the pane background, POC and VA markers, axis labels and legend text, recorded as measured ratios against the 4.5:1 / 3:1 thresholds.
- **Virtualisation and announcement design review** of the table alternative: how 5 000 rows are exposed without flooding the accessibility tree, how live updates are announced without constant interruption (polite live region, coalesced summary announcements rather than per-print chatter), and how the user can freeze the profile to read it.
- Deliverables: `docs/qa/e19-a11y-audit.md` with findings, severity, WCAG 2.2 success-criterion references, screen recordings, and a remediation ticket per finding; plus the axe-core assertions merged into the CI suite.

## Out of scope
- The design-system components' generic a11y (E05/E07) except as composed here.
- Chart-engine-wide a11y patterns (E11) - this audit consumes the established pattern and reports back if it fails for dense histograms.
- Alert and rule UIs consuming profile metrics (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state is axe-clean
  Given SCR-038 in loading, populated, partial, empty, approximated and error states and SCR-039 open
  When axe-core runs in both themes at 100%, 200% and 400% zoom
  Then there are zero serious or critical violations, and any moderate finding is triaged with an owner and a ticket

Scenario: A screen-reader user can find the POC without sighted help
  Given NVDA with Firefox on a populated session profile
  When the tester performs the scripted task "find the POC price and say whether the last price is inside the value area"
  Then the task is completed using announced content only, within the documented time budget

Scenario: Failure case - colour-only encoding is rejected
  Given a mode where POC, value-area membership or delta sign is distinguishable only by hue
  Then the audit records a blocking finding with the WCAG 1.4.1 reference and a remediation ticket is opened before R2 exit

Scenario: Edge case - 5 000 rows do not flood assistive technology
  Given a 5 000-row profile with live updates
  When the table alternative is navigated
  Then rows are virtualised, live updates are announced as coalesced summaries rather than per-print, and navigation stays responsive

Scenario: Keyboard-only operation is complete
  Given keyboard input only
  When the user opens the panel, changes period mode, sets value area to 68, toggles single prints and closes SCR-039
  Then every step is reachable, focus is visible at all times, the dialog traps and returns focus, and no control requires a pointer

Scenario: Reduced motion is respected
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then profile transitions and re-bucket animations are suppressed without loss of information
```

## Technical notes / design
- The audit is run against a build with the `E19-Q03` deterministic fixtures so screen-reader transcripts are reproducible and can be diffed on re-audit.
- Announcement policy is treated as a *design* artefact, not an implementation detail: the audit proposes the coalescing rule (for example, announce POC changes and value-area boundary changes only, at most once every N seconds) and records it in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` if adopted, so E21 and E23 reuse it.
- A "freeze profile" affordance is evaluated explicitly; a continuously mutating table is unreadable with a screen reader, and this is the cheapest remedy.
- Findings are severity-mapped: blocking (prevents task completion or is a serious axe violation), major (task completable but degraded), minor (polish), each with a WCAG success criterion.

## Test plan
- Automated axe assertions become part of the `E19-Q03` nightly run so regressions are caught after this one-off audit closes.
- Manual passes are re-run once after remediation to confirm fixes, with the second transcript attached.
- Third-party or specialist review is optional; if the CDO accessibility lead has capacity, one pass is performed by someone outside the E19 team.

## Security notes
- Screen recordings and transcripts are scrubbed of account identifiers and tokens before being attached to the audit document.
- No production data is used; the audit runs on the fixture stack only.
- Any assistive-technology-only bypass of an authorization state (for example, row content readable when the panel shows an authorization error) is reported as a security finding to `E19-X02`, not only as an a11y finding.

## Accessibility notes
- Success criteria explicitly exercised: 1.3.1 info and relationships, 1.4.1 use of colour, 1.4.3 contrast, 1.4.10 reflow, 1.4.11 non-text contrast, 1.4.12 text spacing, 2.1.1/2.1.2 keyboard and no trap, 2.4.3 focus order, 2.4.7 focus visible, 2.4.11 focus not obscured, 2.5.8 target size, 3.2.2 on input, 3.3.1/3.3.3 error identification and suggestion (row-size clamp message), 4.1.2 name role value, 4.1.3 status messages.
- The table alternative must convey exactly the numbers verified by `E19-Q02`, so accessible content and rendered content cannot diverge.

## Performance notes
- The audit records the cost of the accessible path: the table alternative active must not breach the frame budget, cross-checked against the `E19-Q04` configuration that measures it with a screen reader attached.
- If virtualisation is required to meet both a11y and performance, the chosen approach is documented so later panes do not reinvent it.

## Observability
- Findings are tracked as tickets labelled `a11y` and `area/order-flow`, linked from the audit document and from the E19 epic, so the epic DoD a11y checkbox has evidence behind it.
- The audit document records the exact build sha, browser and AT versions used.

## Definition of Done
- `docs/qa/e19-a11y-audit.md` merged with findings, severities, WCAG references and evidence.
- Zero open blocking findings, or an explicit owner-signed accepted risk recorded on the epic before R2 exit.
- axe-core assertions merged into CI for both screens across all enumerated states.
- Remediation tickets filed and linked; a re-audit pass recorded for every blocking finding fixed.
- Sign-off from the accessibility lead and the E19 frontend lead.

## Dependencies
- `E19-S01`, `E19-S04` (panel behaviour), `E19-D03` (hi-fi design with a11y annotations), `E19-Q03` (deterministic fixtures and axe harness).
- Design-system a11y baselines from E05/E07; engine a11y mirror pattern from E11.

`test/e19-profiles-a11y-audit`

title: Exploratory charters and the E19 profile regression pack
body:
## Context
Scripted suites confirm the behaviours someone already thought of. Profiles are a surface where the interesting defects come from *combinations* nobody enumerated: a swing-anchored profile while replay is scrubbing, a composite spanning a tick-size change, two panes on the same symbol with different row sizes, a preset saved in TPO mode applied to a delta profile, naked POCs accumulating over a weekend of thin trade. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` pairs scripted testing with time-boxed exploratory charters for exactly this reason.

This ticket also assembles the durable regression pack: the subset of E19 checks that must keep running long after R2, because profiles feed alerts and rules and will be silently depended upon by later epics.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Surfaces under charter: SCR-038 profile panel, SCR-039 settings dialog; components CMP-110 ProfileBar, CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane, CMP-184 MarketProfileTpoPane, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge; contracts `GET /market/profile` and WS `profile.{symbol}.{kind}`; stories US-VP-001..US-VP-009.
- **Exploratory charters** in `qa/charters/e19/`, each a 90-minute time-boxed session with a stated mission, coverage area, oracle and debrief notes:
  1. *Period-mode blending* - switch rapidly between composite, session multiples, visible range, personalised range and swing-anchored while data streams; hunt for stale rows, mismatched legends and orphaned POC lines.
  2. *Multi-pane disagreement* - two or more profile panes on one symbol with different `price_grouping`, `value_area_pct` and kinds; hunt for shared-state bleed and contradictory POCs.
  3. *Thin and pathological markets* - a symbol trading at three price levels, a symbol with a single enormous print, a symbol newly listed mid-session.
  4. *Boundary times* - UTC midnight rollover, `funding_8h` anchor crossings, a custom anchor equal to the current time, weekend low-liquidity composites.
  5. *Interaction with replay and recorder* (E26/E16) - scrubbing while a visible-range profile is active, entering replay mid-period, pinning and unpinning recorded symbols.
  6. *Settings and presets abuse* - extreme but legal values (`value_area_pct` 50 and 95, `price_grouping` 1000, `tpo_period_minutes` 1 and 240), preset applied across kinds and symbols, export/import round-trips.
  7. *Long-session soak by hand* - leave a session profile open for a full trading day and inspect for drift against a fresh rebuild at the end.
- **Regression pack** `qa/regression/e19-pack.md`: the durable subset (oracle equality on three canonical fixtures, POC/VA metric publication, axis alignment, partial/approximated states, WS resubscribe equality, preset round-trip) with an owner, a cadence (per-release) and expected runtime.
- **Triage output**: every charter produces bugs or an explicit "no findings" note; findings judged systemic are proposed as new scripted cases in `E19-Q01`/`E19-Q02`/`E19-Q03` so the pack learns.
- A short **heuristics sheet** for profile testing (invariants worth checking anywhere: totals reconcile, POC is inside the value area, VAH >= POC >= VAL, rows are unique per price, sum of buy and sell equals volume, delta equals buy minus sell) reusable by E18, E21 and E23.

## Out of scope
- Automated implementation of newly found cases - charters produce tickets, the owning suites implement them.
- Performance measurement (`E19-Q04`) and the a11y audit (`E19-Q06`), though charters may surface qualitative concerns and hand them over.
- Production monitoring of profiles (E42/ops).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Charters are executed and debriefed
  Given the seven charters in qa/charters/e19
  When each is executed as a time-boxed session against a staging build
  Then each has a written debrief stating coverage achieved, bugs filed and areas deliberately not covered

Scenario: Invariants hold everywhere they are checked
  Given the heuristics sheet invariants
  When they are applied across every charter session
  Then no violation is observed, or each violation is filed as a bug with a reproduction

Scenario: Failure case - a systemic finding becomes a scripted case
  Given a charter finds that swing-anchored profiles lose their anchor after a timeframe change
  Then a bug is filed and a new scripted case is added to the relevant suite, not merely noted in the debrief

Scenario: Edge case - long-session drift
  Given a session profile left open for a full 24 h trading day
  When a fresh rebuild is compared to the live accumulated profile at the end
  Then they are identical, or the difference is filed as a P0 correctness bug

Scenario: Regression pack is executable and owned
  Given qa/regression/e19-pack.md
  When a release candidate is prepared
  Then the pack runs within its stated runtime, has a named owner, and produces a recorded pass or fail
```

## Technical notes / design
- Charters are session-based: the tester records a timestamped log, and the debrief distinguishes setup time, test design time and bug investigation time so coverage claims are honest.
- The heuristics sheet is deliberately generic across order-flow surfaces, because the same reconciliation invariants catch footprint, CVD and profile aggregation bugs, and one shared sheet avoids three divergent ones.
- The regression pack is sized to run inside a release-candidate window; anything slower belongs to nightly rather than the pack.
- Charter 7 (long-session soak by hand) is the only manual-only item that must survive into the regression pack, because it is the cheapest detector of cumulative drift and is not worth automating before E46.

## Test plan
- Two testers execute independently where charters overlap (2 and 4) to measure how much is found by a second pair of eyes; the result informs whether charters continue into R3.
- Every filed bug is verified fixed by the same tester who found it before the epic sign-off in `E19-Q08`.
- The regression pack is dry-run once end to end and its runtime recorded.

## Security notes
- Charters use non-production accounts on staging; the extreme-values charter overlaps with `E19-X02` and any finding with a security flavour (resource exhaustion, authorization bypass, information leak in an error) is routed to Security, not closed as a functional bug.
- Testers are instructed never to paste live API keys or account identifiers into charter notes or screenshots.

## Accessibility notes
- Each charter includes at least ten minutes of keyboard-only or screen-reader-on exploration, so accessibility defects are found by people using the feature rather than only by the formal audit.
- Any a11y finding is cross-filed to `E19-Q06` remediation tracking.

## Performance notes
- Charters record subjective responsiveness and any observed stutter with the conditions that produced it; these observations become candidate scenarios for `E19-Q04` rather than being dismissed as anecdote.
- The long-session charter also records memory growth of the browser tab, which is the most likely home for a profile-related leak.

## Observability
- Debriefs name the build sha, fixtures and environment; bugs carry HAR/WS captures and the `x-request-id` of relevant calls.
- Charter outcomes are summarised in the E19 quality dashboard so exploratory coverage is visible next to automated coverage.

## Definition of Done
- All seven charters executed and debriefed; every finding filed, triaged and either fixed or explicitly deferred with an owner.
- `qa/regression/e19-pack.md` merged with an owner, cadence and measured runtime, and referenced from the release checklist.
- The heuristics sheet merged and referenced by the E18/E21/E23 test plans.
- Systemic findings converted into scripted cases in the owning suites.

## Dependencies
- `E19-Q02`, `E19-Q03` and `E19-Q05` provide the automated baseline so charters spend their time on the unknown rather than re-checking the known.
- Replay/recorder surfaces from E26/E16 for charter 5.

## Branch

## References

- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 9
- `qa/plans/e19-profiles-test-plan.md`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 5 (invariants underpinning the heuristics sheet)

2. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`

Base area for `indicators`: packages/chart-engine/src/indicators/ and services/api/orderflow/
- Surfaces under charter: SCR-038 profile panel, SCR-039 settings dialog; components CMP-110 ProfileBar, CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane, CMP-184 MarketProfileTpoPane, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge; contracts `GET /market/profile` and WS `profile.{symbol}.{kind}`; stories US-VP-001..US-VP-009.
- **Exploratory charters** in `qa/charters/e19/`, each a 90-minute time-boxed session with a stated mission, coverage area, oracle and debrief notes:

body:
## Context

E19 is one of the R2 epics whose output (POC, VAH, VAL as exact metrics) is consumed by later trains, so signing it off loosely would export uncertainty into E40 alerts and the rule engine.

## Scope / Deliverables

  - **Metric publication statement**: `profile_poc`, `profile_vah`, `profile_val` (and HVN/LVN levels) are published with the documented exactness and parameterisation, verified against the oracle, so E40 and the rule engine can depend on them.
- **Epic-level regression and exploratory pass** executed against the release candidate (the `E19-Q07` pack plus a fresh two-hour exploratory session), recorded here rather than only in child tickets.
- **Demo evidence** for the owner acceptance required by the epic DoD: a recorded walkthrough of session, composite, delta and TPO profiles with POC/VA and naked POCs.
- A short **known-limitations** section stating, in user-facing language, the single-step value-area expansion approximation, the approximated-from-bars fallback, recorder-dependent history limits, and the TPO period convention (UTC-anchored, crypto has no RTH).

## Out of scope
- Fixing defects - this ticket reports and blocks, it does not remediate.
- The R2 gate decision itself, which is the PRR's; this supplies its profile input.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Given docs/qa/e19-signoff.md

Scenario: Quality gates are green
  Then profile engine coverage is at least 85 percent, frontend profile module coverage at least 80 percent, there are zero open P0 or P1 bugs against E19, and every accepted deviation is signed by a named owner

Scenario: Failure case - sign-off is blocked by an open P1
  Given an open P1 bug that the profile POC drifts after a tick-size change
  When sign-off is attempted
```
